title: Keep state changes predictable
summary: Reducers should be predictable: the same state and action should produce the same result.
introduction: Reducers should be predictable: the same state and action should produce the same result. Your task: Call the reducer twice with the same inputs and compare.
learningObjectives: Call the reducer twice with the same inputs and compare.

blocks.text: Reducers should be predictable: the same state and action should produce the same result. Create outside facts before sending the action.
Use a JavaScript project with @reduxjs/toolkit installed. React examples also need react-redux and React. These imports require your project build tool and are not available in the plain playground.
Read the code step by step

items: `payload` carries the data supplied with an action, such as an amount or a new record.

blocks.text: The same empty state and action always give a one-item list.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not fetch data, read the clock or generate random ids inside a reducer. Those are outside jobs.

blocks.text: Call the reducer twice with the same inputs and compare.
